newsitem.title: UK: Farringford up after trading resumes.
newsitem.headline: Farringford up after trading resumes.

text.p: Shares in hotel-to-pub-group Farringford Plc rose on Thursday after trading in the stock resumed following its suspension on February 26, 1997.
By 1430 GMT the stock was up 3-3/4p to 15-3/4, retreating from a high at 18-1/2p. The volume was 3.9 million shares.

Trading in Farringford, which will be renamed Arena Leisure Plc, was resumed after Wednesday's EGM approved the purchase of the racecourse Lingfield Park 1991 Limited as well as the measures to raise capital.
Farringford paid 10 million stg for Lingfield by issuing 100 million shares. It bought the majority from TJH Group Limited, Farringford's main shareholder, in a reverse takeover.
In addition Farringford raised another 5.35 million pounds by placing an open offer for 34.5 million shares and offering subscriptions for 19 million shares.
Farringford said on Wednesday 29.1 million shares had been placed already and about 3.5 million shares had been offered by NatWest.
A total of about 160 million shares had therefore been allotted on Wednesday.
